modules.name: Energy and carbon limits (VBBL Part 10 Tables A/B/C, EMG v3.0, rezoning layer)
modules.design_question: Which TEUI, TEDI and GHGI limits does my program mix trigger under VBBL 2025, does my estimate pass and by what margin, and what do rezoning policies add?
inputs: Layer 0: floor area by program tag, mapped to VBBL major occupancy (C, D, E; A, B, F) with user override
Storeys per independent building (tower plus podium count together unless designed as independent structures), user override
Modelled floor area (MFA) per EMG v3.0: excludes indoor parking, includes mechanical and unconditioned space
Permit-date selector (Jan 2022, Jul 2023, Mar 2025, Sep 2025 wording)
Path selector: Table A, Table B (Group C only), Table C (LCES attested with a document), Passive House
TEUI, TEDI, GHGI from P04-M03 EMG mode (or manual entry); PV deduction from P04-M05
Reference-model results for 'all other' occupancies (manual entry in BASIC mode)
outputs: limits registry rows {TEUI, TEDI, GHGI, effective_date, clause, status, source_id}
MFA-weighted whole-building limits plus combined-TEDI and combined-GHGI sub-limits
reference-model GHGI limit for all-other space (0.5 x fossil-only reference)
pass/fail flags and margin (%) per metric, labelled screening
rezoning-layer checklist (GBPR, HBP, SLD, LCES) with status chips
floor-area incentive record for PROG modules
policy-review and by-law 13472 forward-risk flags

parameters.name: Occupancy mapping (major occupancy group)
parameters.relationship: Table A has rows only for Group C, hotel/motel, Group D/E and office. Assembly, care and industrial space (Groups A, B, F) takes a GHGI limit 50% below a fossil-only reference model, so more civic or cultural area forces a reference-model run.

parameters.name: Storeys per building (6 or fewer vs over 6)
parameters.relationship: Group C limits are 110/25 up to 6 storeys and 120/30 above. A tower plus podium classes as one building unless designed as independent structures (10.2.1.1(4)), so every VTC tower lands in the over-6 class.

parameters.name: Compliance path
parameters.relationship: Table B (100/15, GHGI waived) exists for Group C only. Table C relaxes TEUI/TEDI (office 100 to 130, 20 to 30) only when connected to a Low Carbon Energy System; GHGI never relaxes. Passive House replaces the tables.

parameters.name: Permit date / table version
parameters.relationship: Residential over 6 storeys GHGI was 6 and hotel 8 (Jul 2023 to Feb 2025); both fell to 3.0 and 4.0 in the 1 Mar 2025 wording. TEUI/TEDI cells did not change. The by-law in force at permit sets the limit.

parameters.name: Modelled floor area (denominator)
parameters.relationship: Limits and results are per MFA, which excludes indoor parking but includes mechanical and unconditioned space. Parkade energy still counts in the numerator, so each parkade level raises TEUI. MFA must be within 5% of drawing GFA or be explained.

parameters.name: Emission factors
parameters.relationship: GHGI = sum(energy x factor) / MFA, with electricity 0.011, natural gas 0.180 and district energy as agreed by utility and City. Gas emits about 16 times more per kWh, so fuel choice dominates GHGI.

parameters.name: Rezoning policy layer
parameters.relationship: A rezoning must meet GBPR (embodied-carbon report, resilience worksheet, commissioning, sub-metering; energy modelling dropped in the Nov 2024 revision), plus HBP and SLD expectations whose text is unopened. Each becomes a tracked deliverable.

parameters.name: Floor-area incentive
parameters.relationship: City lists +10% floor space for larger buildings meeting ILFI Zero Energy or Passive House (to 31 Oct 2030). It could fund a stricter path; applicability to a tower rezoning is unverified.

metrics.name: TEUI vs MFA-weighted limit
metrics.good: <= weighted limit. Table A (15 Sep 2025): office 100, Group D/E retail 120, hotel 140, residential over 6 storeys 120. Table C (LCES): office 130, retail 170, hotel 170, residential over 6 storeys 130.
metrics.basis: Opened City unofficial wording (S42) and Council VBBL 2025 text (S49); tables identical. Unofficial wording has no legal force; by-law under review (S55).
metrics.method: L = sum(MFA_i x L_i) / sum(MFA_i); margin = (estimate - L) / L; estimate net of on-site PV

metrics.name: TEDI vs MFA-weighted limit
metrics.good: <= weighted limit. Table A: office, retail, hotel 20; residential over 6 storeys 30 (6 or fewer 25). Table C: office, retail, hotel 30; residential over 6 storeys 40. Table B: Group C 15.
metrics.basis: Same sources. Corridor and form adjustments are post-processing credits that EMG requires to be reported before and after.
metrics.method: Area-weighted average; add the combined sub-check below

metrics.name: GHGI vs MFA-weighted limit
metrics.good: <= weighted limit: 3.0 for office, retail and Group C; 4.0 for hotel (Tables A and C, from 1 Mar 2025). Table B path waives GHGI. Energy only; refrigerants reported separately.
metrics.basis: Mar 2025 and Sep 2025 wording (S43, S42). GHGI as defined in EMG v3.0 excludes refrigerants.
metrics.method: GHGI = sum(E_fuel x EF_fuel) / MFA

metrics.name: Combined TEDI sub-check (portions with a table TEDI target)
metrics.good: MFA-weighted TEDI of all occupancies that have a table TEDI target <= their combined TEDI limit, in addition to the whole-building limit
metrics.bad: Sub-check fails while the whole building passes
metrics.basis: Replaces the residential-only sub-limit. EMG s5.1(e) applies to all portions with a TEDI target, excluding reference-model occupancies. Final text unopened.
metrics.method: Separate area-weighted TEDI over occupancies with a table target

metrics.name: Combined GHGI sub-check (portions with an absolute GHGI target)
metrics.good: Combined GHGI of those portions <= their combined limit
metrics.bad: Combined GHGI exceeds their combined limit
metrics.basis: EMG s5.1(e) redline; final text unopened.
metrics.method: Separate area-weighted GHGI over occupancies with an absolute target

metrics.name: GHGI limit for all-other occupancies (Groups A, B, F)
metrics.good: <= 0.5 x GHGI of a fossil-fuel-only reference model (EMG s5.3 shortcut: reference results with gas factor 0.180 for heating, ventilation heating and DHW)
metrics.basis: Table A row (from Jul 2023). Replaces the 2018-20 rule (TEUI 35% better). TEUI/TEDI follow the NECB 2020 or ASHRAE 90.1-2019 reference model: team interpretation of blank cells.
metrics.method: GHGI_limit = 0.5 x sum(reference energy x EF) / MFA

metrics.name: GHGI-R (refrigerants), reported only
metrics.good: Report GHGI-R = GWP x charge x (0.02 L + 0.1) / (L x MFA); no VBBL limit
metrics.bad: Counting GHGI-R inside the Table A limit
metrics.basis: EMG v3.0 defines GHGI-R separately with no compliance requirement (S46). The earlier plan to include it from Jan 2025 was not adopted.
metrics.method: Charge, GWP and service life from P04-M03 inputs

metrics.name: Passive overheating hours (cooling disabled, NRC GW2.0 file)
metrics.good: Report monthly hours above ASHRAE 55 80% limits. 200 h/yr is a team preset for non-mechanically-cooled spaces; 20 h for vulnerable occupants (EMG recommendation).
metrics.basis: EMG v3.0 requires the hours to be reported; the 200 h wording appears only in the redline and the 2018 EMG. BCBC 2024 adds one cool space at 26 deg C per dwelling.
metrics.method: Hourly zone temperature from P04-M03

metrics.name: Forward check: By-law 13472 limits for large existing buildings
metrics.good: 2026: office <= 25, retail <= 14; 2040: GHGI 0 and heat energy intensity <= 0.09 GJ/m2.yr. Lifetime-risk context only.
metrics.bad: Design relies on gas heating that cannot meet the 2040 limit
metrics.basis: Values from the 2022 deck (S02); reference manual unopened. A May 2026 motion proposes pausing Energize Vancouver enforcement (S56).
metrics.method: Compare design GHGI and heat intensity with the schedule

metrics.name: Legacy limit: high-rise residential GHGI 6, hotel GHGI 8
metrics.good: n/a: superseded. Use 3.0 and 4.0 from the 1 Mar 2025 wording; 6 and 8 applied Jul 2023 to Feb 2025.
metrics.bad: Using 6 or 8 for a permit under the 1 Mar 2025 or later wording
metrics.basis: Versioned wordings S05, S43, S42. The earlier 'January 2025' date is corrected to 1 Mar 2025.
metrics.method: Keep visible in the registry in FALSE ASSUMPTION colour

modules.method: 1) Map Layer 0 tags to VBBL major occupancy groups (C, D, E use table rows; A, B, F go to 'all other'); derive storey class per building, with override. 2) Compute MFA per EMG v3.0 (excludes indoor parking, includes mechanical and unconditioned space), within 5% of drawing GFA. 3) Look up limits in a versioned JSON registry keyed by permit date and path (Jan 2022, Jul 2023, Mar 2025, Sep 2025); each cell carries clause, date, source and status. Table C stays locked until the user attests a City LCES recognition document. 4) MFA-weight limits; add combined TEDI and GHGI sub-checks; set the all-other GHGI limit at 0.5 x fossil-only reference. 5) Compare estimates (TEUI net of PV; GHGI energy only; GHGI-R separate); margin = (estimate - L)/L. 6) Show the rezoning checklist and a policy-review banner.
visualization: Three bullet bars (TEUI, TEDI, GHGI): estimate bar, weighted-limit tick, pass/fail badge linked to the clause
Stacked bar of each occupancy's MFA contribution to the weighted limit, with sub-check ticks
Limits registry table with status chips (verified / team assumption / FALSE ASSUMPTION) and a permit-date slider
Timeline 2021-2040: table steps (Jul 2023, 1 Mar 2025, 15 Sep 2025), review report-back 2027, by-law 13472 limit 2040
Rezoning-layer checklist card
modules.human_judgment: Compliance path; how City staff classify cultural, civic, amenity and restaurant space; whether a justified breach is worth arguing; LCES recognition; confirming values with the City and a qualified energy modeller.
modules.limits: Screening, not compliance: formal compliance needs an EMG v3.0 model by a qualified modeller. Wording opened is the City's unofficial consolidation. HBP, SLD, LCES policy and current GBPR text unopened. VBBL is under review (report-back 2027).

modules.name: Massing energy indicators (VFAR, WWR, orientation, thermal bridging)
modules.design_question: How compact, glazed and oriented is my massing, and what does that imply for heating demand (TEDI) before any simulation is run?
inputs: Layer 0 mesh (faces, normals, storey heights) and program tags (parkade excluded from MFA)
True-north rotation from the site plan (its north arrow is rotated from the street grid)
WWR per facade (default preset or imported glazing)
EPW weather file for heating degree days (NRC GW1.0 for EMG-consistent proxy; TMYx optional)
Slab-edge, balcony and spandrel details: psi (W/m.K) x length per storey and effective-U presets (BETBG-style)
Target whole-building airtightness (L/s.m2 at 75 Pa)
Optional: U-value and heat-recovery presets from ADVANCED mode
outputs: indicator set {VFAR, envelope/volume, perimeter/GFA, plate depth, WWR and glazed area by azimuth}
per-storey table
facade-area-by-azimuth grid
TEDI_proxy band (kWh/m2.yr) with calibration status
EMG form-adjustment eligibility flag
perimeter/core zoning and effective-U inputs for P04-M03
glazing areas for CLIM and SPAC modules

parameters.name: Vertical facade area / floor area (VFAR)
parameters.relationship: EMG v3.0 defines VFAR = above-ground wall area / MFA. Higher VFAR raises conduction and infiltration per m2 of floor (TEDI up). EMG allows a TEDI/TEUI adjustment 40 x (VFAR - 0.65), max 20, only where site limits force a slim form.

parameters.name: Window-to-wall ratio
parameters.relationship: Higher WWR raises glazing heat loss (TEDI), solar gain and daylight. The VBBL NECB path caps reference-building WWR at 40% and vertical SHGC at 0.36, so glazing beyond 40% earns no allowance in reference-model comparisons.

parameters.name: Thermal bridging at slab edges, balconies and spandrels
parameters.unit: psi (W/m.K) x m per storey; effective U (W/m2K)
parameters.relationship: EMG v3.0 requires interface-detail heat loss inside effective U-values (BETBG method). These losses were historically underestimated, so clear-field U understates TEDI; detail choices (thermal breaks, balcony removal) change TEDI directly.

parameters.name: Facade azimuth relative to true north
parameters.relationship: Azimuth sets solar gain and glare per m2 of glass. The site plan's north arrow is rotated from the street grid, so grid north would misassign exposure. Size of the effect for Vancouver towers is unsourced.

parameters.name: Floor-plate depth (facade to core)
parameters.relationship: Deeper plates lower envelope per m2 of floor (TEDI down) but cut daylight and natural-ventilation reach. Effect on glazing need and cooling is unsourced and left to P04-M03.

parameters.name: Tower height / slenderness
parameters.relationship: Greater height strengthens stack effect and wind pressure, raising infiltration and corridor-pressurization loads. EMG v3.0 cuts the corridor TEDI/TEUI adjustment maximum from 10 to 5 kWh/m2.yr and removes its GHGI adjustment. Height magnitude is unsourced.

parameters.name: Airtightness target
parameters.relationship: EMG v3.0 converts a targeted whole-building leakage to modelled infiltration (x 0.112, on above-ground wall area). 1.5 is the VBBL test limit and suggested start; below 1.30 needs a sealed narrative. Tighter targets cut TEDI.

metrics.name: Vertical facade-to-floor ratio (VFAR, EMG definition)
metrics.good: Report only; informational line at 0.65 (form-adjustment eligibility, not a pass line)
metrics.bad: VFAR >= 0.65 without site-forced slimness: adjustment not claimable
metrics.basis: EMG v3.0 redline s2.7 and Focal report (S46); final text unopened.
metrics.method: Above-ground wall area / MFA by storey

metrics.name: Envelope-to-floor ratio vs reference box
metrics.good: At or below a reference box of equal GFA and height (relative comparison)
metrics.bad: Above the reference box by more than a user-set tolerance
metrics.basis: No City or code threshold found for towers; a relative comparison avoids inventing an absolute number. Engineering reasoning, not a sourced relationship.
metrics.method: Ratio of design to reference-box value

metrics.name: Whole-building and per-azimuth WWR
metrics.good: <= 40% (reference-building cap, VBBL 10.2.2.3)
metrics.basis: 40% is the sourced NECB-path reference cap; using it as a design target is a team choice. The eSim 57% to 40% case is an example only.
metrics.method: Glazed area / gross wall area by storey and sector

metrics.name: TEDI proxy band vs P04-M01 TEDI limit
metrics.good: Band upper bound <= weighted TEDI limit (A: 20-30; C: 30-40); pass badge greyed until calibrated
metrics.bad: Band lower bound > weighted TEDI limit
metrics.basis: Steady-state proxy is unvalidated; high-gain offices have low balance points. Calibrate per occupancy against P04-M03 runs and show a band, not a point.
metrics.method: Effective UA x HDD plus ventilation and infiltration loss less usable gains, / MFA

metrics.name: Glazing share facing south-west to west
metrics.good: No sourced threshold
metrics.basis: Orientation effect for Vancouver towers not sourced; show as information only.
metrics.method: Glazed area in 202.5-292.5 degree sectors / total glazed area

metrics.name: Effective-to-clear-field U ratio
metrics.good: No sourced threshold: report the ratio
metrics.basis: EMG s3 requires bridged U-values; BETBG psi presets not opened, so presets are team assumptions.
metrics.method: U_effective / U_clear-field by assembly

modules.method: 1) Slice the mesh per storey; classify exterior faces by normal tilt (default 10 degrees) into walls and roof. 2) Rotate normals by the true-north offset and bin into 8 azimuth sectors. 3) MFA = tagged floor area (parkade excluded); VFAR = above-ground wall area / MFA; plate depth = longest facade-to-core distance. 4) Glazing = WWR preset x wall area. 5) Effective U = clear-field U plus psi x length bridging per storey (BETBG-style presets, team assumption until opened). 6) TEDI proxy band = [UA_eff x HDD x 24/1000 + rho.cp x ventilation flow x (1 - SRE) x HDD x 24/1000 + infiltration loss - usable gains] / MFA, HDD from the EPW; show a range from preset bands; recalibrate against P04-M03. 7) Compare every indicator with an equal-GFA reference box; flag VFAR >= 0.65.
visualization: Polar bar chart (8 sectors) of glazed area by solar-exposure class, with true-north and street-grid-north ticks
Radar chart of normalised indicators, design vs reference box
Per-storey line chart (WWR, VFAR, plate depth) beside the 3D massing coloured by facade orientation
Bullet band of the TEDI proxy against the P04-M01 limit with a greyed-until-calibrated badge
modules.human_judgment: Facade composition, glazing versus views, daylight and cultural expression; whether higher WWR is justified by human-scale and City in Nature intent; shading, fin and balcony strategy.
modules.limits: Screening proxy only: no thermal mass, HVAC or stack model. Bridging presets, orientation and plate-depth magnitudes are unsourced. Relative indicators depend on the reference box. Not a compliance calculation.

modules.name: Shoebox energy model: TEUI, TEDI, GHGI and peak loads (EMG mode and Physics mode)
modules.design_question: What TEUI, TEDI, GHGI, peak loads and end-use split do my program and envelope produce, using a transparent sample-storey EnergyPlus model that follows the City guidelines?
inputs: Layer 0 geometry and program tags; MFA per EMG
P04-M02 zoning (perimeter/core), WWR, effective U-values and glazing by azimuth
ADVANCED presets: air-tightness target, heat-recovery SRE and frost control, lighting/plug densities, HVAC type and COP, schedules
Refrigerant type (GWP), charge per kW, service life
DHW demand by occupancy and DHW plant/source
Elevator count, parkade fan and lighting loads
P04-M06 supply option and emission factors
Weather: NRC GW1.0 (EMG mode), GW2.0 (overheating), TMYx or future files (Physics mode)
outputs: Annual end uses by fuel (kWh/yr)
TEUI, TEDI, GHGI, CEDI and GHGI-R by occupancy and whole building, pre- and post-adjustment
Peak heating and cooling loads (W/m2)
Hourly electric and thermal load profiles (8760) for P04-M04, M05, M06
Passive overheating hours per zone

parameters.name: Opaque and glazing effective U-values
parameters.relationship: Lower effective U cuts conductive loss and TEDI; EMG requires bridged U-values. The City's example baseline uses double-pane window wall, so glazing upgrades trade TEDI against enclosure embodied carbon (P04-M07).

parameters.name: Heat-recovery sensible effectiveness and frost control
parameters.relationship: Higher SRE cuts ventilation heating, a large TEDI part. EMG requires SRE with fan-heat treatment and an electric preheat coil if no frost control is specified, so unrealistic recovery is not rewarded.

parameters.name: Airtightness target and modelled infiltration
parameters.relationship: EMG v3.0 models infiltration from the targeted leakage (x 0.112 on above-ground wall area). Leakage below 1.30 needs a sealed narrative. Lower leakage cuts TEDI; fixed height multipliers are not part of EMG mode.

parameters.name: Domestic hot water demand and plant
parameters.relationship: DHW is outside TEDI but inside TEUI and GHGI. EMG sets suite DHW at 0.0016 L/s per person peak, 5 deg C inlet, drain-heat recovery credit up to 15%. Gas DHW alone must stay under about 17 kWh/m2 to meet GHGI 3.0.

parameters.name: Refrigerant type, charge and leakage (GHGI-R)
parameters.relationship: EMG: GHGI-R = GWP x charge x (0.02 L + 0.1) / (L x MFA), reported with no limit. City-study archetypes: central heat pumps 0.2-0.9, 3-pipe VRF 1.7-2.6 kgCO2e/m2.yr, so system type is a carbon decision.

parameters.name: Plant type and efficiency
parameters.relationship: TEDI is independent of plant; TEUI falls with COP. Emission factors are fixed (electricity 0.011, gas 0.180, district per utility), so replacing gas with electricity cuts GHGI about 16-fold per kWh.

parameters.name: Dwelling cooling provision
parameters.relationship: BCBC 2024 (in VBBL 2025) requires one cool space at or below 26 deg C per dwelling. Cooling adds to TEUI and is reported as CEDI, which has no VBBL limit; passively cooled designs previously excluded it.

parameters.name: Vertical transportation
parameters.relationship: EMG models each elevator at 3 kW on the building schedule, with no regenerative credit; the City flagged elevator methodology for future review. Car count from SYST therefore moves TEUI in a 244-305 m tower.

parameters.name: Parkade lighting and fans
parameters.relationship: Parkade lighting (24 h) and fans (4 h/day) count as site energy, but parking area is outside MFA, so each parkade level raises TEUI per m2. This links MOBI parking decisions to energy.

parameters.name: Pool and amenity programme
parameters.relationship: Pool-water heating counts in TEUI and GHGI but is excluded from TEDI under EMG v3.0 definitions; pool-hall space and ventilation conditioning still count in TEDI. A 2018 case had 58% of heating from pools.

parameters.name: Lighting, plug loads and schedules
parameters.relationship: Suite plug load 5 W/m2 (gas cooking splits 1 gas, 4 electric), suite lighting per design up to 5 W/m2, schedules per NECB 2020. Higher gains cut TEDI but raise TEUI and cooling.

parameters.name: Weather file
parameters.relationship: EMG mode uses the NRC GW1.0 future-shifted TMY (energy) and GW2.0 (overheating); Physics mode may use TMYx or future files. Different files shift TEDI, cooling and overheating hours, so results are comparable with limits only in EMG mode.

metrics.name: Modelled TEUI, TEDI, GHGI (EMG mode) vs P04-M01 limits
metrics.good: <= MFA-weighted limits from P04-M01 (and combined sub-limits)
metrics.basis: Limits verified (S42). The model is a screening estimate; Physics mode shows no pass/fail.
metrics.method: EnergyPlus annual results by end use and fuel, with EMG inputs and post-processing adjustments reported pre and post

metrics.name: Passive overheating hours (cooling disabled, GW2.0)
metrics.good: Report monthly hours; 200 h/yr team preset for non-mechanically-cooled spaces; 20 h for vulnerable occupants
metrics.basis: The 200 h value comes from the 2018 EMG via a 2020 paper and the v3.0 redline; confirm hour limit, comfort model and file in the EMG in force.
metrics.method: Hours above the ASHRAE 55 80% limit per zone, cooling disabled

metrics.name: Cooling energy demand intensity (CEDI)
metrics.good: Report only; VBBL has no CEDI limit
metrics.basis: City 2026 study states CEDI is reporting-only; EMG v3.0 defines it.
metrics.method: Annual cooling output per MFA

metrics.name: Peak heating and cooling load density
metrics.good: No sourced threshold
metrics.basis: Reported for sizing and for P04-M04/M06 only. City study archetypes: 27-48 W/m2 (residential, not towers).
metrics.method: Design-day peaks from the model

modules.method: Two modes. EMG mode (the only mode compared with P04-M01): sample-storey Honeybee/OpenStudio models per height band (perimeter depth from P04-M02, core zone) using EMG inputs: NRC GW1.0 weather, NECB 2020 schedules, suite gains and DHW, elevators 3 kW, infiltration from target leakage (x 0.112), effective U, SRE-based HRV, factors 0.011 and 0.180 (district per utility). Scale by storey count; add podium, retail, amenity, parkade and plant zones. Apply corridor and form adjustments as post-processing and report pre and post. TEDI = space and ventilation heating before plant efficiency; GHGI = sum(fuel x EF)/MFA; GHGI-R and CEDI reported separately. Physics mode (exploratory, no pass/fail): TMYx or future files, stack/wind multipliers, 8760 export. Fast mode: surrogate over presets, labelled.
visualization: Sankey diagram of end uses by fuel
Monthly stacked bars of heating, cooling, lighting, plant
Heat-balance waterfall (losses and gains per m2)
Parallel-coordinates plot of design options with limit bands (EMG mode only)
8760 false-colour heatmap of electric load (day vs hour, kW legend)
modules.human_judgment: Selecting archetype assumptions, plant and refrigerant strategy, schedules and acceptable overheating; interpreting results against policy; deciding when a qualified modeller must replace the screening model.
modules.limits: Sample floors miss podium-tower coupling and detailed plant. Only the v3.0 redline and recommendations report were opened, not the final guideline; NRC GW1.0/GW2.0 file availability unverified. Not compliance-grade. Physics-mode multipliers are unsourced; surrogate accuracy untested.

modules.name: Electrical peak demand and utility capacity
modules.design_question: What peak electrical demand will the tower place on the grid, when does it occur, and is that plausible for downtown Vancouver supply?
inputs: Layer 0 GFA by program
P04-M03 hourly electric loads (profile mode) or electrified-load presets (preset mode)
P04-M06 supply option (heat pump vs district steam)
Parking stalls and EV share (MOBI)
Vertical transportation and life-safety loads (SYST), optional
User-entered BC Hydro service allocation
outputs: peak_kW and peak_kVA (assumed power factor)
hourly_load[8760]
winter-peak and summer-peak share, load factor
load-duration curve
service-size flags for SYST (transformer room)

parameters.name: Demand density by use (electrified-load presets)
parameters.relationship: Peak scales with area times density. No Vancouver-sourced values were found, so presets (heat pump at design-day COP, unit cooling, EV) are labelled team assumptions until a utility or engineer supplies values.

parameters.name: Heating electrification (heat-pump COP, backup)
parameters.relationship: Electric heat moves load to cold winter evenings. A City study found service sizing follows the larger of heating or cooling load in efficient buildings (gas heating cut a fourplex service 3%). District steam moves the peak upstream.

parameters.name: Cooling electrification
parameters.relationship: BCBC 2024 requires one cool space per dwelling, adding a summer coincident peak that heat-pump heating does not offset. It sets service size when cooling load exceeds heating load.

parameters.name: Coincidence / diversity factor
parameters.relationship: Total peak is below the sum of use-wise peaks. The Canadian Electrical Code accepts a 'demonstrated load' (24 months of measured W/m2) in place of calculated load when a qualified person does the calculation.

parameters.name: EV charging stalls and kW per stall
parameters.relationship: Each stall adds charger kW to the coincident peak unless managed. CE Code Rule 86-300 recognises load management, and the CBO may set minimum EV energy-management performance, so managed charging can cut service size.

parameters.name: Thermal storage / load shedding
parameters.relationship: Storage shifts heating or cooling electricity out of the peak and lowers kVA, at the cost of plant space. Effect size is project-specific.

metrics.name: Peak demand vs confirmed service allocation
metrics.good: <= allocation confirmed by BC Hydro (user input)
metrics.basis: No public allocation rule found; downtown context: Dal Grauer replaced by West End substation (as early as 2032), Murrin by East Vancouver (as early as 2031). City staff say the CBO can make allowances if BC Hydro cannot serve.
metrics.method: Peak of aggregated hourly load / power factor

metrics.name: Demand density vs reference ranges
metrics.good: Within user-selected reference range
metrics.basis: CE Code Table 14 office basic load of about 50 W/m2 (lighting and receptacles only) is quoted by a forum post and not confirmed; McFadyen's tables unopened.
metrics.method: Peak kW / GFA by use

metrics.name: Multi-unit residential planning demand (Toronto Hydro, context only)
metrics.good: No pass/fail. Context: class average under 200 units 166; 200-500 units 410; over 500 units 903
metrics.basis: Toronto planning values (Sept 2025), end uses not stated; an all-electric Vancouver supertall with cooling will exceed them by design, so transfer is unverified.
metrics.method: Show beside the residential block peak as a reference line only

metrics.name: Winter-peak share of annual peak
metrics.good: No sourced threshold
metrics.basis: Information only; Creative Energy says it is considering how its systems can ease winter peaks.
metrics.method: Share of top-1% hours falling in Dec-Feb

modules.method: Two modes. Preset mode: peak_i = A_i x density_i (electrified-load presets, editable, team assumption) x coincidence factor; sum; add EV (with optional load-management factor), vertical transport, cooling and plant; kVA = kW / power factor. Profile mode: take hourly electric loads from P04-M03, add heat-pump or electrode-boiler electricity from the P04-M06 choice and EV schedules, aggregate to 8760 hours, then find peak, load factor, winter and summer peak shares and the load-duration curve. Compare with the user-entered service allocation. A context card cites BC Hydro's substation replacements, VBBL 10.3.1.1 (service capacity per the Electrical Safety Regulation) and tells the user to confirm interim capacity with BC Hydro.
visualization: 8760 heatmap (day vs hour) with a kW colour legend
Load-duration curve with the confirmed service allocation as a horizontal line
Stacked bars of coincident peak by use
Grid-context card linking the BC Hydro and provincial sources
modules.human_judgment: Negotiation with BC Hydro, service voltage and redundancy, diversity factors and demonstrated-load claims by an electrical engineer, backup generation and storage choices.

modules.name: On-site PV potential (roof and facade) and its TEUI credit
modules.design_question: How much electricity can roof and facade PV realistically supply on a shaded supertall, how much TEUI does it remove under the City guidelines, and where is PV worth installing?
inputs: Layer 0 roof planes and facade faces with normals
Context massing (existing and approved towers) from SITE modules for shading
Weather file (EPW, dataset reported)
Usable-area fractions (mechanical, terraces, setbacks)
P04-M03 hourly electric demand and MFA
Module efficiency and loss presets
outputs: PV area and kWp by surface class
Annual and hourly PV generation
Specific yield (kWh/kWp.yr) by surface class
PV share of annual and midday demand
TEUI deduction (kWh/m2 MFA.yr) passed to P04-M01
Irradiance map for CLIM and PRES modules

parameters.name: TEUI credit under EMG
parameters.relationship: EMG defines TEUI as site energy minus on-site renewable generation, per MFA, so PV lowers TEUI directly. The v2.0 rule that 7% on-site generation zeroes the electricity factor sits in a section marked deleted in v3.0; GHGI credit is unresolved.

parameters.name: Usable roof fraction
parameters.relationship: Mechanical plant, amenity terraces and setbacks reduce PV area. A supertall's roof is small relative to its total floor area, so roof PV covers a small share of annual use; the tool calculates the share.

parameters.name: Surface tilt and azimuth
parameters.relationship: Yield per kWp falls from optimally tilted surfaces to vertical east, west and north facades. pvlib computes plane-of-array irradiance for any tilt and azimuth, so the ranking is calculated rather than assumed.

parameters.name: Shading from context towers
parameters.relationship: Neighbouring 244-305 m towers shade lower facades and sometimes roofs; loss is computed hourly by ray casting from the context massing.

parameters.name: Weather dataset
parameters.relationship: The 2026 TMYx release takes solar radiation from ERA5, so yield differs from older files; EMG compliance runs use the NRC GW1.0 file. Report the dataset used and keep PV and demand on the same file.

parameters.name: Module efficiency and system losses
parameters.relationship: Higher efficiency raises kWp per m2 of surface; temperature, soiling and inverter losses scale output. Defaults are editable presets, not sourced values.

parameters.name: Demand profile
parameters.relationship: PV fraction falls as tower demand rises relative to roof area. Midday office loads coincide with PV; winter evening heating and residential loads do not.

metrics.name: Annual PV generation and specific yield
metrics.good: No sourced threshold: report values and rank surfaces
metrics.basis: No Vancouver-specific benchmark opened; NRCan PV potential maps were not reachable.
metrics.method: pvlib transposition plus PVWatts-type chain on hourly EPW

metrics.name: TEUI credit from PV (deduction in M01)
metrics.good: Report deduction = PV kWh / MFA; no cap found in the EMG definition
metrics.bad: No threshold; a deduction that is not sited and sized in the design is not claimable
metrics.basis: EMG v3.0 TEUI definition (redline and Nov 2024 draft); cap, metering and the Roof Mounted Energy bulletin unopened.
metrics.method: Annual PV kWh consumed or exported / MFA

metrics.name: PV share of annual electricity use
metrics.good: User-set target (no sourced target; no code requirement for on-site renewables found)
metrics.basis: No VBBL requirement for on-site generation found in Part 10 text (S42).
metrics.method: Annual PV kWh / annual electricity kWh from P04-M03

metrics.name: Surface ranking by yield
metrics.good: Top-ranked surfaces by computed yield
metrics.bad: Surfaces below the cut-off the user sets
metrics.basis: Cut-off is a user preset; no sourced viability threshold.
metrics.method: Sort surfaces by annual irradiance after shading

modules.method: 1) Extract roof planes and facade faces from Layer 0; apply usable-fraction presets. 2) Read EPW irradiance. 3) For each surface compute plane-of-array irradiance with pvlib transposition models, with hourly shading from context massing by ray casting. 4) Convert to AC output with a PVWatts-type model using editable efficiency, temperature coefficient and loss presets. 5) Sum by surface class and compare with hourly demand from P04-M03 for annual and midday PV fraction, self-consumption and export. 6) Rank surfaces by yield so facade BIPV suitability is calculated. 7) Show PV share next to total tower demand so the supertall reality is visible. 8) Pass annual kWh / MFA to P04-M01 as a TEUI deduction, shown separately; flag GHGI treatment unresolved.
visualization: False-colour irradiance map on roof and facade meshes (kWh/m2.yr legend) with PV-suitable surfaces outlined
Monthly bars of PV generation vs demand
Ranked bar chart of specific yield by surface class
Hourly overlay of PV and demand for a winter and a summer week
TEUI bar with PV deduction shown as a separate segment
modules.human_judgment: Whether PV is architecturally acceptable on facades or the crown, BIPV aesthetics, structural and maintenance access, and whether on-site generation is worth the carbon and cost.
modules.limits: Yield depends on weather dataset and context-shading quality; no verified Vancouver benchmark. Facade PV economics, wind loads and glare not covered. The EMG GHGI treatment of PV and any cap on the TEUI credit are unverified. Loss and efficiency defaults are presets.

libraries.role: Sky-view and shading analysis (Radiance licence not checked here)

modules.name: District energy and low-carbon energy system (LCES) connection
modules.design_question: Can the tower connect to a recognised low-carbon energy system, and what does that do to its limits, GHGI and electrical peak?
inputs: P04-M03 heating, hot-water and cooling energy and peak loads
Supply option selector (all-electric heat pump, district steam/hot water, hybrid)
Utility-confirmed district emission factor and efficiency (user entry)
LCES attestation: City recognition document reference and utility letter (user entry)
Site location (Layer 0 / SITE modules)
outputs: Option comparison {TEUI, TEDI, GHGI, electric peak}
Selected path (Table A or Table C, Table C locked by default) for P04-M01
District-supply emission factor record
Heat-density and service-availability flags
Draft low-carbon energy supply study inputs (SLD deliverable if it applies)

parameters.name: LCES recognition (Table C relief)
parameters.relationship: Table C lifts TEUI/TEDI limits (office 100 to 130 and 20 to 30; residential over 6 storeys 120 to 130 and 30 to 40) only for a building connected to an LCES; GHGI does not relax. Default off until the user attests City recognition.

parameters.name: District steam status (Creative Energy)
parameters.relationship: City letter (2021): planned electrode boilers of at least 10 MW would qualify as an LCES if built as planned. Before approvals and construction start, applications must also show a viable on-site LCES, plus written utility confirmation of connection and carbon intensity.

parameters.name: District emission factor
parameters.relationship: The factor is set per project by the utility and the City; no steam factor was found. EMG lets heat be modelled as delivered at 100% efficiency or the whole district system be included at the utility-agreed efficiency.

parameters.name: Connection availability
parameters.relationship: Downtown has no forced-connection by-law; the utility expands opportunistically, so a tower must confirm availability. The plant was announced for roughly 12 million ft2 of new development shared among projects (2021, status unverified).

parameters.name: Heating peak density
parameters.relationship: A higher heating peak needs more steam or hot-water capacity from a finite plant and, if all-electric, a larger electric winter peak (P04-M04).

parameters.name: On-site and nodal systems (heat pump, geo-exchange, sewer heat)
parameters.relationship: The VBBL LCES definition includes on-site systems that supply mostly renewable, highly efficient heat. Whether an all-electric heat-pump plant qualifies depends on the LCES policy (unopened); nodal systems pair heat pumps with geo-exchange and sewer heat.

parameters.name: SLD low-carbon energy supply study
parameters.relationship: If the Sustainable Large Developments policy applies (critic: sites of at least 0.8 ha or 45,000 m2; unverified; the VTC block is 1.15 ha), a low-carbon energy supply feasibility study becomes a rezoning deliverable fed by this module.

metrics.name: Limit relief when LCES-attested (Table C minus Table A)
metrics.good: LCES attested with document and GHGI <= limit
metrics.bad: Relies on TEUI/TEDI relief without attestation, or GHGI > limit
metrics.basis: Table values verified in S42 and S49 (relief: office +30/+10, retail +50/+10, hotel +30/+10, residential over 6 +10/+10; no relief for 6 or fewer). LCES recognition itself unverified.
metrics.method: Difference of table cells per occupancy; applied only after attestation

metrics.name: GHGI by supply option
metrics.good: <= P04-M01 GHGI limit
metrics.basis: Limit from P04-M01; electricity 0.011 and gas 0.180 verified in EMG; district factor is a user entry, unsourced.
metrics.method: Delivered energy x factor per option / MFA

metrics.name: Plant capacity headroom
metrics.unit: MW or m2 of new development
metrics.good: Project demand within capacity the utility confirms
metrics.basis: The 12 million ft2 figure is from 2021 announcements; the City letter gives at least 10 MW; 2026 commissioning status was not found.
metrics.method: User-entered utility letter value vs project load

modules.method: 1) Take annual heating, hot-water and cooling energy and peaks from P04-M03. 2) For each supply option (A all-electric heat pump, B district steam or hot water, C hybrid with heat recovery and peaking), compute delivered energy by fuel using editable efficiencies and distribution losses; electricity 0.011, gas 0.180, district factor entered from the utility. 3) Re-evaluate TEUI, TEDI and GHGI. Option B is shown against Table A with the user's factor; Table C is unlocked only when the user attests City LCES recognition and cites a document. 4) Compute the added electric peak (heat pump at design-day COP vs upstream electrode boiler). 5) Raise flags for heat density and service area; the user attests availability. 6) Output an option comparison with source badges and draft inputs for the SLD energy study.
visualization: Three option cards (A, B, C) with GHGI bars against the limit tick and a Table A / Table C (locked) badge
Sankey of heat sources to end uses for the selected option
Bar pair showing winter electric peak with and without district supply
Site pin against a service-area polygon when the user uploads one
modules.human_judgment: Negotiating connection and tariff with the utility, obtaining the City's LCES recognition, accepting dependence on a district plant, and whether heat-pump nodes or district steam better fit the project.
modules.limits: The decarbonised plant's 2026 status, capacity and factor are unverified. LCES policy text, SLD policy and EMG final text unopened. District factors are user inputs. The site is hypothetical, so real service areas may not apply.

modules.name: Embodied carbon at massing stage (VBBL 10.4, National wbLCA Guide + City Addendum)
modules.design_question: Will the tower's embodied carbon meet Vancouver's current Part 3 limit (2 x benchmark, intensity or baseline path), and which structure and envelope choices move it most?
inputs: Layer 0 GFA excluding parkade; storeys above and below grade
Structural system preset from STRC (concrete core with flat slab, steel composite, mass-timber hybrid) and spans
Envelope type and glazing from P04-M02/M03
Parkade levels and stalls from MOBI
User-typed material carbon factors or EPD values (Reported GWP), with the user's own licence attestation
Compliance-path selector (intensity or baseline) and permit-date selector
outputs: EC intensity (kgCO2e/m2 GFA) and total (tCO2e) by element (substructure, shell) and stage A1-C4
Intensity-path limit and baseline-path limit (factor f = 2, plus optional ILC)
Pass/fail against the regime in force at the permit date, plus an unadopted-2025 scenario overlay
Lever ranking (what-if deltas) for STRC and SPAC
Embodied Carbon Design Report draft fields

parameters.name: Compliance path (intensity vs baseline)
parameters.relationship: Intensity path limit is 800 kgCO2e/m2 of GFA regardless of height or parkade. The baseline path compares with a functionally equivalent copy and removes parking, height, soil and shape variables, so deep parkades and supertall structure favour the baseline path.

parameters.name: Structural system and material intensity
parameters.relationship: Structure and substructure dominate upfront carbon, so concrete mix, rebar and the concrete/steel/timber choice move the result most. A City 33-storey tower study gives about 468 kgCO2e per m2 above-grade floor area (team arithmetic); presets are team assumptions with ranges.

parameters.name: Concrete SCM content and strength
parameters.relationship: Raising SCM from 10% to 35% (GU to GUL cement) cut a 33-storey concrete tower's GWP by 22.6% in the City study; the City example baseline uses 15% SCM, so more SCM lowers A1-A3 against it.

parameters.name: Below-grade parking levels
parameters.relationship: Parkade structure counts in the assessed object but its area is outside GFA, so each level raises kg/m2. Baseline parking may follow Addendum defaults (e.g. 54.73 m2 per space, office tower); halving parkade saved 6% in the City study.

parameters.name: Facade system and glazing
parameters.relationship: The City example baseline is double-pane window wall; in the City study, steel-stud double-glazed walls cut 11% against curtain wall and triple glazing added 2%. Read P04-M02/M03 and M07 together.

parameters.name: Height and lateral system
parameters.relationship: Taller towers need larger lateral systems and foundations; encapsulated mass timber is limited to 18 storeys, so a supertall is a hybrid. Quantity change per metre is unsourced: label presets team assumption with a range.

parameters.name: Product-specific EPDs and procurement
parameters.relationship: The proposed design may use manufacturer EPDs while the baseline uses industry averages, which widens the reduction. Reported GWP must be used, not uncertainty-adjusted GWP, and the same tool data for both.

parameters.name: Missing life-cycle stage placeholders
parameters.relationship: Only when a tool lacks a whole stage: A4 4%, A5 6%, B1-B5 10%, C1-C4 5% of A1-A3. Stage choices shift totals directly; the placeholders are not recommended once optional scope is included.

parameters.name: Industry Leadership Credits (ILC)
parameters.relationship: Optional reporting and reuse credits raise the limit factor to f + ILC (up to 2.05), relaxing the limit. Appendix I of the Addendum is a draft and unopened.

parameters.name: Short-cycle biogenic carbon
parameters.relationship: Only short-cycle biogenic material (growth cycle of 10 years or less, waste, salvage, residues) may be deducted for compliance; other biogenic carbon, carbonation and Module D are reported separately, so long-rotation timber cannot offset the total.

metrics.name: Embodied carbon vs intensity-path limit (A1-C4, required scope)
metrics.good: <= 800 (2 x 400 x GFA); up to 820 with maximum ILC
metrics.bad: > 800 fails this path only; check the baseline path
metrics.basis: VBBL 10.4.1.2 (15 Sep 2025) sets 'double an acceptable benchmark'; Addendum v1.0 sets ECI 400 and f = 2 (S49, S50, S51). Unofficial City wording; values may be refined.
metrics.method: EC_P (A1-C4, substructure + shell, minus short-cycle biogenic) / GFA excl. parkade

metrics.name: Embodied carbon vs baseline-path limit
metrics.good: Design <= 2.0 x functionally equivalent baseline (plus ILC)
metrics.basis: Same sources; baseline built with City default assumptions and Addendum parking defaults.
metrics.method: EC_P / EC_baseline; baseline uses same tool, scope and 60-year period

metrics.name: Unadopted 2025 tightening (scenario overlay only)
metrics.good: Scenario: <= 360 (380 with maximum ILC) or at least 10% below baseline; 6-storey wood -20%; responsible-materials option
metrics.bad: Above the scenario line: no pass/fail, shown as forward risk
metrics.basis: Sept 2024 staff deck proposed it; City ZEB page lists the 2025 reductions as delayed; next update TBD (2027). Not in 10.4.1.2.
metrics.method: Overlay lines on the stacked bar; no badge

metrics.name: 2030 city-wide aspiration (40% below 2018)
metrics.good: <= 240 (0.6 x 400 benchmark)
metrics.basis: The 40% is a Climate Emergency Action Plan city-wide target; 240 is arithmetic on the 400 benchmark, which may not equal the 2018 baseline.
metrics.method: Compare intensity with 0.6 x benchmark

modules.method: Massing-stage estimator, not a compliance tool. 1) GFA excluding parkade; parkade structure kept in the assessed object. 2) Required scope: substructure and shell (superstructure, exterior vertical and horizontal enclosure); interiors and services optional. 3) Quantities = area x intensity preset by STRC system (team assumption with range) or user EPD entries (Reported GWP); no ICE data bundled or queried. 4) A1-A3 plus A4-A5, B1-B5, C1-C4 from entered data or Guide placeholders (4/6/10/5% of A1-A3, only if a stage is missing). 5) Benchmark: intensity path 400 x GFA, or functionally equivalent baseline (City defaults, Addendum parking). 6) Limit EC_L = benchmark x (2 + ILC); deduct short-cycle biogenic carbon. 7) Select regime by permit date; overlay unadopted 2025 lines as scenario. 8) Report Module D separately. Flag that permits need the City Design Report, raw tool data and listed tools.
visualization: Stacked bar by element and life-cycle stage with the 800 intensity line, the baseline x 2 line and a dashed unadopted-360 scenario line
Waterfall of reduction levers (SCM, slab type, facade, parkade, procurement) with City-study magnitudes marked
Sankey from material to element to total
Pass/fail badges linked to the clause; colour marks EPD-backed values vs presets
modules.human_judgment: Defining the functionally equivalent baseline, structural material strategy, treatment of short-cycle biogenic carbon, selecting EPDs and reuse evidence, and judging whether a low-carbon structure is buildable at supertall height.
modules.limits: Massing-stage estimate; intensity presets are placeholders with ranges, no supertall benchmark opened. The City requires listed tools (rezoning: One Click LCA Carbon Designer, Embodied Carbon Pathfinder, C.Scale; permit: Athena, tallyLCA, bimCAT, EC3, One Click LCA) and its Design Report; this tool is none of them. By-law and benchmark may change.

modules.name: Whole-life carbon summary (illustrative; operational + embodied)
modules.design_question: Over a 60-year life, how do operational and embodied carbon compare, and which design lever cuts whole-life carbon most?
inputs: P04-M03 annual energy by fuel and MFA
P04-M06 supply option and emission factors
P04-M05 PV generation
P04-M07 embodied carbon by stage and GFA
Study period and stated grid-factor scenario
MFA/GFA ratio for denominator conversion
outputs: Whole-life carbon intensity (kgCO2e/m2 GFA) and total (tCO2e)
Operational vs embodied split
Lever ranking across modules
Board-ready carbon summary data for PRES

parameters.name: Study period
parameters.relationship: A longer period multiplies operational carbon (GHGI x years) but not embodied carbon; the City's guide fixes a 60-year lifespan for embodied-carbon studies.

parameters.name: Grid emission factor scenario
parameters.relationship: BC electricity is 0.011 kgCO2e/kWh in the EMG (BC Hydro to be 100% clean by 2030), so operational carbon is small and embodied carbon dominates. State the scenario; constant factors are not forecasts.

parameters.name: Supply mix (electric, gas, district)
parameters.relationship: Gas or district-steam share raises operational GHGI roughly in proportion to its factor times delivered energy (gas 0.180 vs electricity 0.011); set through P04-M06.

parameters.name: Refrigerant leakage (GHGI-R)
parameters.relationship: GHGI-R is reported outside the VBBL limit, so M08 adds it to operational carbon to keep it visible; over 60 years 0.2-2.6 kgCO2e/m2.yr is 12-156 kgCO2e/m2, so high-charge VRF matters.

parameters.name: Replacement cycles and service lives (B4)
parameters.relationship: Shorter component service lives raise stage B; the placeholder is 10% of A1-A3 when a tool lacks data.

parameters.name: Biogenic carbon and carbonation
parameters.relationship: Only short-cycle biogenic carbon may be deducted for compliance (M07); other biogenic carbon and carbonation are shown separately and are not netted off the whole-life bar.

parameters.name: Denominator conversion (MFA vs GFA)
parameters.relationship: GHGI is per MFA and embodied carbon per GFA excl. parkade. Scale operational by MFA/GFA (EMG tolerates 5% vs drawings) or report totals in tCO2e, so the sum is not mixed-denominator.

metrics.name: Whole-life carbon intensity (illustrative sum at limits; no pass/fail)
metrics.good: No threshold. Illustration: current limits 800 + 3.0 x 60 = 980; unadopted-2025 scenario 360 + 180 = 540. Not a target.
metrics.basis: Arithmetic on sourced limits at constant factors; denominators converted via MFA/GFA. LETI and RIBA numbers not extracted.
metrics.method: EC intensity + sum over years of (GHGI + GHGI-R) x MFA/GFA

metrics.name: Operational share of whole-life carbon
metrics.good: No sourced threshold
metrics.basis: Information only; at the GHGI limit operational carbon over 60 years (180) is about 18% of 980 or 33% of 540.
metrics.method: Operational / whole-life

metrics.name: Embodied carbon vs 2030 aspiration
metrics.basis: See P04-M07; derived from the 40%-by-2030 city target.
metrics.method: Compare with 0.6 x 400

modules.method: 1) Operational: annual GHGI per fuel from P04-M03 and P04-M06 times study years, with a stated grid-factor scenario (default constant EMG factors). 2) Add GHGI-R from P04-M03 as a separate operational term. 3) Show the PV offset from P04-M05 at the grid factor separately. 4) Embodied: A1-C4 intensity from P04-M07 (short-cycle biogenic deducted as in M07); Module D, other biogenic and carbonation shown separately. 5) Convert both terms to one denominator (GFA excl. parkade) with MFA/GFA, or show tCO2e. 6) Whole-life = embodied + operational; no pass/fail. 7) Lever ranking: re-run P04-M03/M07 deltas (glazing, structure, supply) and rank by kgCO2e/m2 saved. 8) Export numbers and source ids to PRES.
visualization: Stacked bar: embodied (A1-A5, B, C) plus operational over 60 years, with M01 and M07 limit markers (no ceiling label)
Cumulative carbon timeline (year 0 to 60) showing embodied spike and operational ramp
Lever bar chart ranked by kgCO2e/m2 saved
Board-ready summary tile with source badges
modules.human_judgment: Study period and grid scenario, how to value biogenic carbon, trading operational against embodied carbon, and how to present the result for the jury.
modules.limits: Aggregates uncertain inputs; no sourced whole-life threshold. Grid factors beyond today are scenarios, not forecasts. Inherits all M03/M07 limits and excludes fit-out and MEP embodied carbon unless the user adds them.

flags.claim: High-rise residential GHGI limit is 6 kgCO2e/m2.yr and hotel GHGI is 8 (2020-2023 tables, 2020 case study, ZEBX primer)
flags.correction: Under the 1 Mar 2025 wording and the 15 Sep 2025 VBBL, residential over 6 storeys is 3.0 and hotel 4.0 (Tables A and C). 6 and 8 applied Jul 2023 to Feb 2025.
flags.detail: Older values remain visible in the registry in FALSE ASSUMPTION colour. Verified r1 in S42, S43, S05.

flags.claim: The ICE database can be used freely for project embodied-carbon calculations in the tool
flags.correction: ICE Educational V5.0 is educational-only; non-educational use is not permitted after 30 Sep 2026 and it cannot be used in tools or reporting.
flags.detail: Do not bundle or query ICE in the hosted tool at all; accept only user-typed factors with the user's licence attestation. Use EC3 data (account, attribution, limits) or user values.

flags.claim: Vancouver requires new towers to cut embodied carbon by 40%
flags.correction: The 40% is a city-wide 2030 target in the Climate Emergency Action Plan. The by-law limit is 2 x a benchmark (VBBL 10.4.1.2); the proposed 2025 reductions are delayed.
flags.detail: The tool shows the 40% line as a team-assumption aspiration only.

flags.claim: Tower dwellings can rely on passive cooling if overheating stays under 200 hours
flags.correction: BCBC 2024 (in VBBL 2025) requires at least one cool space at or below 26 deg C in every dwelling, so passive-only dwellings are not allowed.
flags.detail: EMG v3.0 still requires passive overheating hours to be reported with cooling disabled; the 200 h limit wording is unverified in the final guideline.

flags.claim: By-law 13472 limits (office 25, retail 14 kgCO2e/m2.yr) govern a new tower's permit
flags.correction: They apply to existing office and retail buildings over 100,000 ft2 from 2026; new towers are governed by VBBL Part 10 and the rezoning policy.
flags.detail: Used only as a forward-looking risk indicator (2040 limit GHGI 0, heat energy intensity 0.09 GJ/m2.yr); enforcement may be paused (May 2026 motion).

flags.claim: Current energy rule for cultural/civic ('all other') space is the 2018-20 rule (TEUI 35% better than baseline, TEDI and GHGI equal to baseline)
flags.correction: Table A (from Jul 2023, unchanged in Mar and Sep 2025): GHGI limit is 50% below a fossil-fuel-only reference model; TEUI/TEDI follow the NECB 2020 / ASHRAE 90.1-2019 reference model (EMG s5.1-5.3).
flags.detail: The 35% saving came from the 2017/2018 rezoning policy. Superseded for current permits; kept visible as FALSE ASSUMPTION.

flags.claim: Assembly, care and industrial (Group A, B, F) GHGI must be 85% below a fossil-fuel-only reference from Jan 2025 (City 2022 deck; round-1 critique)
flags.correction: The adopted VBBL Table A (Mar 2025 and Sep 2025) says 50% lower; EMG s5.3 example also uses 0.50.
flags.detail: The 85% step was approved in principle in 2022 but is not in the by-law text opened; the critique correction was itself corrected against primary text.

flags.claim: In a mixed-use building only the residential portion must separately meet its own TEDI limit
flags.correction: All portions with a table TEDI target must meet their combined TEDI target, and portions with an absolute GHGI target their combined GHGI target, in addition to whole-building limits (EMG s5.1(e)).
flags.detail: The residential-only check in the eSim case arose because residential was the only portion with a TEDI target there.

flags.claim: Embodied carbon above 800 kgCO2e/m2 fails in any case
flags.correction: 800 (2 x 400 x GFA) is the intensity-path limit only. The baseline path allows up to 2 x a functionally equivalent baseline, which can exceed 800 for a supertall.
flags.detail: Also, 800 was the Oct 2023 cap; the current by-law uses factor f = 2 on either benchmark.

flags.claim: The 2025 embodied-carbon limits (360/320 absolute; 10% or 20% reduction plus responsible-materials option) are in force and 'verified'
flags.correction: VBBL 10.4.1.2 (15 Sep 2025) and Addendum v1.0 set f = 2 (limit = 2 x benchmark). The 2025 reductions were proposed, then listed by the City as delayed; next update TBD.
flags.detail: The tool shows 360 / -10% only as an unadopted scenario overlay with no pass/fail. Sources: S49, S50, S52, S54.

flags.claim: The 2021-table TEUI/TEDI values and the Jan 2025 GHGI step were 'verified' from a consultant page and a 2022 deck
flags.correction: Values are now verified in the City's wordings: GHGI steps took effect in the 1 Mar 2025 wording (not January 2025); TEUI/TEDI cells unchanged since Jan 2022.
flags.detail: The label was premature in the first draft; fixed by opening S42-S44, S49.

flags.claim: GHGI-R (refrigerant leakage) counts inside the GHGI limit from January 2025
flags.correction: EMG v3.0 defines GHGI-R as a separate metric with no compliance requirement; Table A GHGI covers energy only.
flags.detail: The City planned inclusion from Jan 2025 (Focal report background), but the consultant recommended and v3.0 adopted separate reporting. Final text unopened.

flags.claim: The City halved the TEDI/TEUI corridor-pressurization credit (complete description of the change)
flags.correction: EMG v3.0: the TEDI/TEUI adjustment maximum falls from 10 to 5 kWh/m2.yr and the GHGI adjustment is removed.
flags.detail: Per Focal recommendations; the redline text interleaves old and new, so the final wording is unopened.

flags.claim: District steam connection qualifies as an LCES and earns Table C relief
flags.correction: Only conditionally: the 2021 City letter recognises planned electrode boilers if built as planned, not for permits before approvals and construction start, and with written utility confirmation. Default off in the tool.
flags.detail: Plant status in 2026 not found. Table C relief is locked until the user attests a City recognition document.

flags.claim: Active cooling is required in every room of every dwelling (26 deg C, windows closed) from 1 Jan 2025
flags.correction: BCBC 2024, adopted in VBBL 2025, requires at least one cool space at or below 26 deg C per dwelling at summer design temperature.
flags.detail: Earlier City deck and Focal report wording was broader; the by-law clause itself was not located in Division B text.

flags.claim: Pool and amenity space raises TEDI sharply (58% of heating from pools)
flags.correction: Under EMG v3.0 definitions pool-water heating, DHW and humidification are excluded from TEDI; they count in TEUI and GHGI. Pool-hall conditioning and ventilation heating still count in TEDI.
flags.detail: The 58% figure is a 2018-20 case under older rules.

flags.claim: Biogenic carbon is excluded from compliance, so timber storage cannot offset the compliance total
flags.correction: Short-cycle biogenic carbon (growth cycle 10 years or less, waste, salvage, residues) may be deducted for compliance; other biogenic carbon, carbonation and Module D are reported separately.
flags.detail: Addendum v1.0 s4.4(a). Long-rotation timber does not qualify.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy sustainability clause, current Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings text, Sustainable Large Developments policy (applicability and low-carbon energy study) and LCES policy text

flags.claim: The Nov 2024 GBPR revision (energy modelling dropped from rezoning applications) was adopted as proposed
flags.detail: Seen only in Council report RTS 16492; the City ZEB page lists the 2023 policy as a previous version, which suggests adoption. Current text unopened.

flags.claim: EMG v3.0 final text details: PV effect on GHGI, corridor GHGI adjustment, infiltration tiers, 200 h overheating limit
flags.detail: Only the redline (old and new interleaved) and the Focal recommendations report were opened; the final PDF is 403.

flags.claim: Creative Energy's electrode boilers are commissioned and have spare capacity for the VTC site
flags.detail: City letter (2021) confirms at least 10 MW planned; 2021 announcements anticipated 2024 commissioning and capacity for about 12 million ft2; no 2026 status or steam emission factor found.

flags.claim: BC Hydro can serve a tower of roughly 100,000 m2 at the site without delay
flags.detail: No public capacity data. Dal Grauer is being replaced by West End (as early as 2032), Murrin by East Vancouver (2031). City Electrical By-law and BC Hydro large-load process unopened.

flags.claim: Energize Vancouver (By-law 13472) enforcement is paused

flags.claim: The +10% floor-space incentive for larger buildings meeting ILFI Zero Energy or Passive House applies to a CD-1 tower rezoning
flags.detail: The City page lists it to 31 Oct 2030; the bulletin and zoning mechanism were not opened.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy Review may add sustainability or energy requirements for towers
flags.detail: Phase I ran Apr-May 2026; policy approaches are shared in early 2027; the page lists no requirements, so limits may change after the competition.

flags.detail: Staff report back in 2027; the by-law is unchanged meanwhile. Limits shown are as of 15 Sep 2025 wording and may not match a later permit.

flags.claim: Whether an all-electric heat-pump plant counts as an on-site LCES for Table C
flags.detail: The VBBL definition includes on-site systems supplying mostly renewable, highly efficient heat; the LCES policy that applies it is unopened.

flags.claim: WWR preset of 40% as the good/bad line
flags.detail: 40% is the sourced reference-building cap on the NECB path (VBBL 10.2.2.3); using it as a design target is a team choice. Editable.

flags.detail: No Vancouver-sourced values found; all are editable presets or user inputs.

flags.detail: Arithmetic on sourced numbers (0.6 x 400; 800 + 3.0 x 60; 360 + 3.0 x 60); not regulatory values and shown without pass/fail.
